newsitem.title: UK: EU's Brittan says UK work hour exemption not easy.
newsitem.headline: EU's Brittan says UK work hour exemption not easy.

text.p: European Commission vice president Sir Leon Brittan said on Monday it was "not going to be easy" for the UK to persuade the rest of the European Union to allow it be exempt from EU rules limiting working hours.
The European Court is due on Tuesday to announce whether it will uphold an EU directive limiting the compulsory working week to 48 hours, a move vigorously opposed by the British government.

Brittan told a Confederation of British Industry conference that the British government would be able to ask for the Maastricht Treaty to be amended to exempt Britain from the directive and similar directives in the future.

The UK would have to "show flexibility itself and accommodate the concerns of other countries when it comes to Treaty changes" if it was to succeed in winning exemption from the work hour rules, he said.

Britain's European partners are increasingly uncomfortable about its exemption from most of the Social Chapter,which the British government argues has been major factor in job creation and the attraction of foreign investment.

Brittan said a number of Treaty changes would be in the UK's own interests, notably updating the Commission's negotiating powers on trade, where he said the EU's hands were "tied too tightly in negotiating issues such as services liberalisation and intellectual property."
